title: How the Internet Delivers Your Request

scenes.say: Ever wondered what actually happens when you open a web page? Let’s break down the journey your request takes across the internet.

scenes.label: DNS
scenes.sub: Resolves the domain name to an IP address
scenes.say: First, your browser uses DNS to turn the website name into an IP address. Without DNS, you’d need to memorize numbers instead of names.
Next, your computer opens a TCP connection, negotiates encryption with TLS, then sends an HTTP request for the page.

scenes.label: Firewall
scenes.sub: Controls which traffic is allowed through
scenes.say: Along the way, firewalls check if your connection is allowed. If the rules block it, your request never reaches the server.
Most web traffic uses TCP for reliability. UDP is faster but skips error checking—great for things like DNS or streaming.

scenes.question: Ping works but HTTP times out. Why?
scenes.right: A firewall blocks the port or the app isn’t listening
scenes.say: Here’s a classic interview trap: If ping works but the app port times out, the network path is fine. The real issue is a firewall or the app isn’t running.
